question.text: The governing documents of a domestic Cat III AIF (trust form) are, in DECREASING order of primacy for an investor, generally:

answer.text: Trust Deed → Investment Management Agreement → Private Placement Memorandum → Contribution/Subscription Agreement
PPM → Trust Deed → IMA → Subscription Agreement
Subscription Agreement → IMA → Trust Deed → PPM
IMA → PPM → Trust Deed → Subscription Agreement

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Hierarchy: Trust Deed (constitutional document setting up the fund) is foundational; IMA (Trustee-Manager contract) derives from the Trust Deed; PPM (offering document) flows from both and governs investor-facing disclosures; Subscription Agreement (investor-specific contract) is the most granular. Higher documents override lower. **The Trap:** Other orderings reverse primacy. PPM cannot override the Trust Deed; Subscription Agreement cannot override IMA terms in a conflict. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A/B/C/D cover the same hierarchy. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** When drafting side-letters with anchor investors, check that any 'enhanced terms' (lower fee, preferred redemption) do not conflict with Trust Deed or PPM — or disclose the side-letter in the PPM as permitted variance.
